positions.commentary: The speaker cites Uber and Lyft as examples of markets where people debated the lack of network effects, yet market caps show a winner-take-all outcome.
The speaker notes that Google was debated for years early on regarding whether it had real network effects or just brand effects.

thesis: The episode argues that market capitalizations often reveal a winner-take-all outcome in markets where network effects were previously debated, citing Uber, Lyft, and Google as examples. It suggests that early skepticism regarding whether these companies possessed true network effects versus mere brand effects was ultimately resolved by their market valuations.
